commands.review_summary:
The branch changes the default OpenClaw target to `2026.7.2-beta.2`, adds setup-wizard reload recovery coordination, makes compact labels culture-invariant, and expands setup, tray, connection, and E2E coverage.

Reproducibility: yes. for the remaining merge blocker: current-head CI reproduces it in all three official-artifact setup E2E shards when the native wizard waits for its Gateway response. The underlying core correction is not yet in a published artifact.
commands.review_followup: - [P1] A maintainer must choose the prerelease-default policy; automated repair cannot produce valid official-artifact proof for an upstream correction that has not shipped.

target.title: fix: stabilize OpenClaw beta setup and PT-PT formatting
target.body:
## Summary

- **Problem:** the Windows Companion still targeted an old OpenClaw package, compact-number labels were culture-sensitive, and the Companion-owned native wizard path did not survive the Gateway reload/reconnect lifecycle required by current OpenClaw beta setup.
- **Why it matters:** Windows users need the Companion to remain the owner of WSL, Gateway service lifecycle, Windows Node, and MXC while OpenClaw owns the native onboarding wizard. Losing the Gateway or recovery state during that handoff strands fresh setup and repair.
- **What changed:** target official OpenClaw `2026.7.2-beta.2`; format compact labels deterministically under `pt-PT`; coordinate reload capture, suspension, recovery, reconnect, revocation, completion, and cleanup; align `wizard.start` with the released empty-object contract; extend focused and E2E coverage.
- **User impact:** the Companion side now preserves and restores Gateway reload state, reconnects deterministically, and keeps setup/recovery ownership explicit instead of relying on sleeps or hidden custom runtime behavior.
- **What did NOT change:** no OpenClaw core patch is vendored here; no token, secret, model, memory, agent policy, permission default, network destination, or command authority changes.

This is intentionally a beta-target PR. Selecting a prerelease as the Companion default remains a maintainer release-policy decision.

## Change Type (select all)

- [x] Bug fix
- [ ] Feature
- [x] Refactor
- [x] Docs / instructions
- [x] Tests / validation
- [ ] Security hardening
- [ ] Chore / infra

## Scope (select all touched areas)

- [x] Tray / WinUI UX
- [x] Windows node capability
- [ ] Local MCP / `winnode`
- [x] Gateway / connection / pairing
- [x] Setup / onboarding
- [ ] Permissions / privacy / security
- [x] Tests / CI / docs

## Linked Issue/PR

- Related #1000
- Related openclaw/openclaw#108435
- Core owner-boundary fix: openclaw/openclaw#110382
- [x] Related to a bug or regression

## Ownership and supported path

- The Windows Companion owns WSL creation, systemd/service lifecycle, Windows Node bootstrap, setup progress, and MXC integration.
- OpenClaw owns the native onboarding wizard and Gateway command runtime.
- The Companion calls released `wizard.start` with an empty parameter object; it does not invent protocol fields.
- Official beta.2 is installed through the normal Companion-owned path. A separately built corrected OpenClaw package was used only in disposable proof after official beta.2 reproduced the upstream Gateway-loss defect; that package is evidence for #110382, not hidden behavior in this PR.

## Validation

Current published head: `312abc2314c29ff3455d25a1785c1a47efae71d2`, normally merged with Windows Node main `277936553135c819d39c464adf706e6074474109` without rebase or force.

Fresh exact-head local proof:

- Official repository build: all `5/5` projects passed.
- Explicit `pt-PT` culture regressions: `3/3` passed for context-window, workspace-size, and dashboard-token compact labels.
- Complete SetupEngine suite: `683/683` passed.
- Complete Tray suite: `1831/1831` passed in a fresh disposable data/temp root.
- Shared: `2908` passed; `31` explicit integration skips.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD`: passed.
- Whole-branch scoped OpenClaw Auto-review against current `origin/main`: zero accepted/actionable findings, `patch is correct`, confidence `0.86`.

Failed-first local proof: the first sandboxed Tray rerun inherited operator AppData and a reused test-output ACL, causing environmental `UnauthorizedAccessException` failures. Redirecting every OpenClaw data and Windows temp root to a unique disposable directory removed 18/19 failures; the remaining atomic-key collision passed alone, and a second full run passed `1831/1831`. No product code was changed for that environment failure.

Fresh GitHub CI on this exact head is the current repository authority.

## Real behavior proof

- Disposable Companion-owned WSL revocation/reconnect E2E passed `1/1` on integrated head `9c308f0b` after the corrected OpenClaw core package was explicitly injected.
- Strict Gateway -> Windows Node -> MXC E2E passed `2/2` without skip allowance on the same integrated head, including protected-write denial.
- Both proof runs installed official beta.2 first, completed uninstall, and removed their temporary WSL distros.
- Official unmodified beta.2 first reproduced the Gateway-loss defect during the native wizard. The passing proof therefore validates the Companion lifecycle against the proposed core correction; it is not presented as proof that the current official beta.2 package already contains that correction.
- Previous GitHub E2E artifacts independently reproduced the new Companion cleanup defect across setup-connect, revocation-recovery, and network-recovery. The earliest exception and path were identical in all three shards; the 19 scenario failures were cascades from one missing-parent-directory bug.

Not verified / pending:

- Fresh exact-head GitHub CI and official beta.2 E2E on `312abc23` are running.
- Exact official published OpenClaw package containing the #110382-equivalent wizard-runtime correction, without injection.

## Failed-first evidence

- Stable `2026.7.1` and official beta.2 exposed different upstream blockers; they were kept separate from Companion ownership bugs.
- The beta.2 native wizard failure was isolated to OpenClaw's Gateway-hosted CLI runtime and moved to the core owner boundary in #110382 rather than patched into the Companion.
- Reload lifecycle review found multiple related edges. They were consolidated into one invariant covering live-mode capture, persisted recovery before suspension, exact-once restoration ownership, disconnect-before-restart, terminal-error restoration, target-aware cleanup, and post-restart completion.
- GitHub workflow `29659705388` then exposed a missing fresh-profile case not represented by local fixtures. The first new unit test also failed because `SetupContext` materialized the directory; the fixture was corrected to remove only its isolated temporary directory and reproduce CI exactly. The production fix itself did not change during that correction.

## Security Impact (required)

- New permissions/capabilities? No
- Secrets/tokens handling changed? No
- New/changed network calls? No
- Command/tool execution surface changed? No
- Data access scope changed? No
- Risk + mitigation: the setup flow temporarily changes Gateway reload mode. Recovery metadata is bounded, persisted before mutation, tied to the exact distro, restored through one owned task, and retained on ambiguity. The new cleanup catch accepts only missing file/directory paths; authorization and other I/O failures still surface.

## Compatibility / Migration

- Backward compatible? Yes for Companion state and recovery marker shape.
- Config/env changes? No operator-managed config migration.
- Migration needed? No.
- Release compatibility: the selected beta package still depends on the separately tracked OpenClaw wizard-runtime correction for the complete supported path.

## Review Conversations

- [x] The recurring reload-lifecycle findings were addressed as one invariant rather than independent patches.
- [x] The prior GitHub E2E failures were downloaded, reduced to their earliest common exception, and corrected with a focused regression.
- [x] The current-head diff received a fresh scoped Auto-review after the correction.
- [ ] Maintainer decision remains required for the prerelease-default policy and the linked core fix.

## Agent Transcript

<details>
<summary>Sanitized multi-day operator/agent engineering record</summary>

This section is a trimmed public record generated from bounded local Codex session transcripts and the verified engineering ledger. Raw logs, tool outputs, system/developer instructions, local paths, credentials, tokens, private messages, and unrelated work were excluded.

### 1. Problem framing and operator constraints

- The work began as a Windows Companion catch-up: retain the Companion-owned Windows/WSL/MXC installation model, add deterministic `pt-PT` formatting, and move the bundled OpenClaw target forward.
- The operator repeatedly clarified the product boundary: this is not a generic Linux install. The Companion must remain the owner of the WSL distro and Windows Node/MXC lifecycle; OpenClaw remains the owner of Gateway and the native wizard.
- The operator rejected hidden runtime substitution and required official-package installation first, disposable proof environments, full failed-first disclosure, durable error tracking, and upstream PRs split by repository ownership.

### 2. Upstream drift and contract reconciliation

- Source review compared current Windows Node main, current OpenClaw source, released stable/beta packages, setup schemas, and the real Companion call path.
- An early design considered forwarding `installDaemon`; current OpenClaw's closed `wizard.start` schema did not support that field. The final Companion path uses the released empty-object contract instead of extending the protocol from the downstream repository.
- When `2026.7.2-beta.2` became available, the operator selected it as the target. The branch was integrated with current Windows Node main so newer upstream pairing and telemetry work was preserved rather than duplicated.

### 3. Companion implementation and review loop

- Compact-number labels were made culture-invariant so `pt-PT` and other decimal-comma locales render deterministic values.
- Setup work then covered Gateway reload capture/suspension, persisted recovery, reconnect, revocation recovery, completion ordering, and cleanup.
- Review found related lifecycle defects over several passes: stale completion, configured-vs-live reload state, ambiguous cleanup, task ownership, restart-before-disconnect, terminal errors that stranded reload mode at `off`, and absent config materialized as an explicit value.
- Instead of treating these as unrelated lint fixes, the work was consolidated into one reload-lifecycle invariant and re-proven across focused tests, complete SetupEngine/Tray suites, official build, and scoped Auto-review.

### 4. OpenClaw core owner boundary

- Official beta.2 installed through the normal Companion path but the Gateway disappeared during the native wizard.
- Investigation isolated the root cause to Gateway-hosted wizard commands using normal CLI exit behavior inside the shared OpenClaw process.
- That correction was separated into OpenClaw core PR #110382. The Companion branch did not vendor or silently carry it.
- For disposable integration proof only, the flow installed official beta.2 and then injected the separately built corrected core package. Revocation/reconnect passed `1/1`; strict Gateway -> Windows Node -> MXC passed `2/2`, including the protected-write denial; cleanup removed both temporary distros.

### 5. Repository proof and GitHub feedback

- Before the latest CI pass, the published branch had passed official build `5/5`, SetupEngine `682/682`, Tray `1825/1825`, Shared `2901` plus `31` explicit skips, and a whole-branch Auto-review with zero findings.
- ClawSweeper correctly kept the PR blocked on two public proof boundaries: official beta.2 still lacks the core correction, and passing integrated proof used an explicitly substituted corrected package.
- The operator chose to publish the coherent beta-target branch for official CI rather than continue speculative local polishing, while keeping those boundaries explicit for maintainers.

### 6. Fresh CI defect and current correction

- GitHub's repository test job, hygiene, and setup gate passed, but all three E2E shards failed before their scenarios started.
- Redacted artifact analysis found one common earliest failure: `cleanup-distro` called marker deletion on a fresh profile where the parent `OpenClawTray` directory had never existed, producing `DirectoryNotFoundException`.
- The fix catches only missing-file and missing-directory cases, preserving fail-closed behavior for permission and genuine I/O errors.
- The first regression attempt exposed a test-fixture assumption because `SetupContext` creates the directory. The fixture was corrected to remove only its isolated temporary directory and reproduce CI faithfully.
- Current result: focused cleanup tests `4/4`, full SetupEngine `683/683`, `git diff --check` clean, and scoped Auto-review zero findings with `patch is correct` at confidence `0.94`. Commit `b570bf42` was then pushed without force for fresh GitHub CI.

### 7. Operator/agent contribution record

- Operator decisions set the target release, insisted on Windows/Companion ownership fidelity, prohibited hidden custom production packages, required disposable validation and public proof, and chose when the branch was coherent enough for official CI.
- Agent work performed source/docs reconciliation, isolated worktree implementation, test and E2E orchestration, artifact triage, scoped Auto-review, owner-boundary separation, PR/issue linkage, and durable failed-first recording.
- No operator runtime, memories, agents, tokens, credentials, or private data are included in this record or changed by the final CI correction.

### 8. Current-main integration and explicit locale proof

- Current Windows Node main was merged normally without rebase or force; no conflict required a product change.
- Three explicit `pt-PT` culture tests now prove decimal-comma locales still render invariant compact labels.
- Fresh current-head build, SetupEngine, Tray, Shared, diff-check, and whole-branch Auto-review gates passed before publication.
- Official-artifact E2E remains intentionally separate: this update does not claim beta.2 contains the unmerged OpenClaw core correction.
</details>
